summary: Michael Como works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under advisers Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt, as well as Kuo-liang Wang. He held a post at Columbia University (attested 2009).

Michael Eido Luetchford is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned an Electronic Engineering degree at the University of Bradford (c. 1964–1967) and studied under the traditional teacher Gudō Wafu Nishijima (c. 1993–2007).

Michael Friedrich is a sinologist who completed his PhD at the University of Munich by 1984, where he was a Wissenschaftlicher Assistent (1983–1986). He later served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.

Michael Hahn specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After studying under Wilhelm Rau and earning a PhD at the University of Marburg (1965–1967), he held professorships at the University of Bonn and Marburg (1988–2007).
Michael Hookham is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa in 1965 and Dilgo Khyentse, and he founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt specializes in Indology and linguistics. He completed his BA (c. 1976–1980) and doctorate (c. 1980–1984) at the University of London, later serving as Head of the South Asia Department and Associate Dean at SOAS.

Michael J. Walsh works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a B.Soc.Sc. at the University of Cape Town, an M.A. at UC Santa Barbara, and completed doctoral studies under William F. Powell (c. 1994–2000).

Michael Janda is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Jochem Schindler and Heiner Eichner, earning a PhD from the University of Vienna (c. 1991–1996) and his Habilitation from Zurich. In 2002, he took a chair at Münster.

Michael Jansen specialized in archaeology and history. He studied at Bonn, Sapienza, Delhi, the ASI, and RWTH Aachen (Promotion c. 1974–1979). He was an architecture dean and urban history professor at Aachen and founding rector at GUtech.

Michael Jay Sweet worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and served there as a clinical assistant professor in psychiatry (attested 1996, 2006).

Michael Jerryson specialized in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Harold Scheub, later serving as faculty at Eckerd College (c. 2010–2013) and Youngstown State University (c. 2013–2021).
Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

Michael L. Walter was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied under Larry William Moses. He served as a Research Fellow at Lumbini International Research Institute (attested 2000) and Special Languages Cataloger at Indiana University.
Michael M. Broido is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge (c. 1963–1967) and held an academic post at the University of Oxford.

Michael Oppitz is a scholar of Tibetology. He held an appointment at the Institute for Advanced Study, Berlin (c. 1987–1988) and served as director (Leiter) at the University of Zurich from around 1991 to 2008.
Michael P. Berman works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2012, he served as a professor at Brock University and as managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.

Michael Puett is a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (c. 1987–1994) studying under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu, and became a professor at Harvard University.

Michael Pye is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Educated at Cambridge and Leeds, he taught religious studies at Leeds, Lancaster, and the University of Marburg, where he was a professor from 1982 to 2004.

Michael R. Sheehy specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under Steven D. Goodman and held research and directorship posts at the University of Virginia (attested 2019).

Michael Radich works in Buddhist studies and sinology. After earning his PhD at Harvard (c. 2001–2007) under Robert M. Gimello, he taught at Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017) and became Professor of Buddhist Studies at Heidelberg in 2018.
